_about: ALL USER-FACING WORDING (foundation 3): one key, one text; read through text_(key, vars) in core.js, whose copy tools/words.js --write keeps. {name} is filled from vars. Owner-edited text that lives in sheets stays there.

words.mail-attempts-kid-body: {said}If that was {first}, "New PIN" on their card on your account gives them a new one at once. If it was not, tell us.
words.mail-attempts-own-tail: If that was not you, reply here.
words.mail-attempts-said:
Somebody has tried the {brand} PIN for {who} {n} times and got it wrong.

Signing in is held up for a minute, and for longer on each wrong answer after that.
words.mail-child-made-body:
Hello,

{first} has made an account on {brand} and gave this address as their grown-up's, because they have no email of their own.

Their account works already. If that is right, open this link to confirm your address (it also puts them on your {brand} parent account if you have one and have confirmed it):

{link}

They sign in with their handle, {handle}, and the PIN they chose. Once you have opened the link, "Forgotten your PIN?" sends a new one to this address if they forget it.

If you have an {brand} parent account on this address and have confirmed it, opening the link also puts {first} on it. If you do not know who this is, ignore this email and nothing happens.
words.mail-confirm-body:
Hello {first},

Confirm your email address by opening this link:

{link}

You can already sign in with this email address{handleSaid} and the PIN you chose — the link only confirms the address is yours. Until it is opened we send nothing else to this address.

If you did not make this account, do not open the link: use "Forgotten your PIN?" with this address instead — it takes the account over and signs everyone else out.
words.mail-confirm-parent-next: Once you have opened the link, your child makes their own account; find their handle on Student profiles and tap Add as my child, and they say yes.
words.mail-invite-body:
Hello {first},

An account has been made for you on {brand}.

Sign in at {site} with your email (or your handle, @{handle}) and the PIN {pin}

Change the PIN under Settings → Signing in.
words.mail-move-body:
Hello,

Somebody signed in to an {brand} account has asked to use this email address for it.

If that was you, open this link on a phone or computer where you are signed in to that account:

{link}

Until it is opened, the account keeps its old address — sign in with that, or with your handle. The link works for {days} days.

If it was not you, ignore this email. Nothing changes, and the link does nothing for anybody who is not signed in to that account.
